title: Deal acceleration playbook and enterprise messaging + security FAQ
author: Maya Patel
body:
Purpose:
This document is a single-source playbook for GTM and sales engineering when engaging enterprise prospects for Redwood Inference. It combines positioning and messaging for buyer personas, competitive battlecards, a repeatable POC and deal-acceleration checklist, pricing guidance and negotiation guardrails, a compact pitch-deck outline, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this to shorten sales cycles, reduce back-and-forth on security questions, and align SDR/AE/SE actions during evaluation windows.

Executive summary:
- Redwood Inference sells a production-first inference platform (hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private deployment) that optimizes latency, cost, and reliability for LLM-powered features.
- This playbook focuses on enterprise deals (>= $50k ARR) that require SLA, audit evidence, and predictable capacity.
- Primary win themes: predictable economics, deployment flexibility (hosted -> dedicated -> private), and production observability (token-level cost tracing, rollouts, regressions).

Elevator pitches (30s):
- For Engineering Leaders: "Ship LLM features reliably — Redwood gives predictable latency and token economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, plus observability to catch regressions before customers do."
- For Platform/Infra: "Standardize inference across teams with a single runtime and rollout tooling — same API, consistent metrics, and fine-grained cost controls for tenant isolation."
- For Security/Compliance: "Private control plane, KMS integrations, and audit-grade logs let you run sensitive workloads on-prem or in a customer VPC while preserving developer ergonomics."

Positioning by persona (key messages and proof points):
- Engineering / ML Engineers:
  - Message: predictable throughput and latency with model lifecycle controls.
  - Proof points: per-route latency SLOs (e.g. p95 < 120ms for curated models on Dedicated), continuous batching and KV cache to reduce token cost by 10–40% depending on workload.
- Platform / Infra:
  - Message: unified runtime across environments reduces operational variance.
  - Proof points: identical API surface, automated fallbacks to compatible model variants, autoscaling policies tied to commit tiers.
- Product / PMs:
  - Message: deliver differentiated LLM features faster and retain cost control.
  - Proof points: referencing two-week POC -> production patterns and built-in quality monitoring / eval integrations.
- Security / Legal:
  - Message: private deployment option, SOC 2 controls, encryption in transit and at rest, KMS/HSM support, and full audit logging.
  - Proof points: sample SOC2 report page, example audit-log retention policies, and customer reference (see case study).

Competitive battlecards (short form):
- General cloud AI endpoints (major cloud provider managed endpoints):
  - Differentiator: Redwood focuses on inference economics + unified runtime for private/hybrid deployment; better tools for rollouts and regression detection.
  - Pressure points: cloud endpoints may win on raw model variety and account consolidation; emphasize Redwood's predictable throughput and cost controls.
- LLM API providers (hosted-first vendors):
  - Differentiator: Redwood offers Dedicated pools and Private deployment for customers who need isolation or committed throughput.
  - Pressure points: hosted-only providers can be simpler for small teams; push on enterprise risk and SLO guarantees.
- Inference infra vendors / self-hosted runtimes:
  - Differentiator: Redwood bundles runtime optimizations + orchestration + support + observability; less engineering lift than building in-house.
  - Pressure points: very large infra orgs may want full control — for those, highlight Redwood Private packaged options and on-prem support agreements.

Suggested rebuttals / objection scripts:
- "We can build this ourselves": 
  - Response: Building a runtime with production-grade autoscaling, KV cache, quantization profiles and rollouts is typically 9–18 months of focused effort. Redwood reduces time-to-production risk and provides measurable cost and latency telemetry out-of-the-box.
- "We are worried about data residency":
  - Response: We offer VPC/private control plane and on-prem packaging. We integrate with cloud KMS and support region-specific hosting for EU/APAC.
- "How do you handle model regressions?":
  - Response: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt/eval sets and raises regression alerts tied to rollouts. We support canary and auto-fallback policies to reduce customer impact.

Deal acceleration playbook (16-week enterprise cadence — condensed):
1) Discovery (week 0–1):
   - Owner: AE + SE.
   - Actions: capture business KPI (latency targets, cost targets, SLA needs), compliance constraints, expected QPS and peak bursts, preferred deployment mode.
   - Deliverable: Discovery memo (1 page) and preliminary sizing estimate.
2) Proposal & POC scoping (week 1–2):
   - Owner: AE + Solutions Architect.
   - Actions: define POC success criteria (latency, throughput, integration points), sample dataset rules, data handling plan (PII scramble or synthetic).
   - Deliverable: POC plan and timeline (max 4 weeks).
3) POC execution (week 2–6):
   - Owner: SE + Customer Eng.
   - Actions: run POC in Hosted or Dedicated sandbox, run load profile, collect latency/cost traces, validate SDK integration.
   - Success criteria (example): sustained p95 latency < target; per-token cost within 10% of estimate; no unresolvable quality regressions for key prompts.
4) Commercial & Security review (week 6–10):
   - Owner: AE + Legal + Security Eng.
   - Actions: lock down commercial terms, review DPA and SOC2 evidence, finalize procurement timelines and SOW.
5) Pilot -> Ramp (week 10–16):
   - Owner: Customer Success + SE.
   - Actions: production cutover plan, rollback policies, SLA handover, train internal ops.

POC checklist (must-have items):
- Sample traffic generator and expected QPS profile.
- Representative prompt set and evaluation harness.
- Performance trace access (token-level cost + latency heatmaps).
- Security review package (DPA, SOC2 summary, network diagrams).
- Contact list for escalation and support SLA.

Pricing guidance and negotiation guardrails (framework, not fixed price list):
- Pricing pillars:
  - Hosted (usage-based): per-token generation/embedding rates with tiered volume discounts. Ideal for fast time-to-value and small-to-medium workloads.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed GPU pools with guaranteed throughput and burst capacity add-ons. Best for predictable, high-volume inference.
  - Private (VPC / on-prem): platform fee + deployment/setup + optional support contract. For regulated / air-gapped customers.

- Commercial play examples (anchor figures are illustrative ranges for negotiation; adjust with finance guidance):
  - Small enterprise POC (3–6 months): Hosted credits + implementation services ($25k–$75k total TCV).
  - Mid-enterprise (Dedicated small commit): $20k–$60k/month committed for predictable throughput.
  - Large enterprise / Private: Multi-month onboarding + platform fee $200k+ and support retainer.

- Discount guardrails:
  - Volume discounts: predefined breaks at 100k, 1M, and 5M monthly tokens for hosted volume.
  - Committed-term discounts: 10–30% off list for 12–36 month reserved Dedicated contracts.
  - Giveaways: implementation credits or extended trial (time boxed), not unlimited usage.
  - Escalation path for exceptions: require approvals from Sales Ops and VP Sales for any > 35% discount or early termination concession.

Pitch deck outline (10–15 slides recommended):
1) Title & hook: quick problem statement and proof point (latency/cost).
2) Customer pain: common infra/ops problems with existing inference (cost surprises, rolling upgrades, regressions).
3) Redwood solution: product overview (hosted/dedicated/private, runtime + console).
4) How it works: runtime + routing + caching + rollout diagram (textual diagram ok).
5) Performance & economics: sample benchmarks, cost delta examples for common workloads.
6) Security & compliance: deployment modes, KMS, audit logs, SOC2.
7) Case study highlight: concise success metrics.
8) POC plan & timeline: what we deliver in 4 weeks.
9) Pricing snapshot & next steps.
10) Appendix: deeper tech proofs, integration checklist.

One-page case study (sales-ready — useable as customer-facing collateral with permission):
- Customer: FinTech SaaS (anonymized: "LeadingPaymentsCo")
- Problem: inconsistent latency during peak billing window and cost overruns when using naive autoscaling.
- Solution: Deployed Redwood Dedicated pool + KV caching + prefix caching for session prompts; integrated with existing SSO and KMS.
- Outcome: p95 latency reduced from 430ms to 95ms during peak; per-token cost reduced by 28% due to caching and batching; 99.95% availability during billing cycles.
- Contact / reference: Customer success path available upon approval.

Security FAQ for prospects (short-form answers for AEs/SEs):
- Q: Where is my data stored and how do you support region controls?
  - A: Hosted offerings are region-aware and can be constrained to US/EU/APAC regions. Dedicated and Private give you full control of physical placement. We publish our region list in the deployment guide.
- Q: Do you provide a private control plane or on-prem deployment?
  - A: Yes — Redwood Private provides a customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem package) with optional air-gapped installation for regulated workloads.
- Q: How is data encrypted?
  - A: All data in transit uses TLS 1.2+; data at rest is encrypted (AES-256). For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM.
- Q: What audit evidence do you provide?
  - A: SOC 2 Type II report summary, system architecture diagrams, and audit-log exports (SIEM-compatible JSON). Full reports provided under NDA.
- Q: How do you handle PII / redaction?
  - A: PII policies are handled via ingestion rules (can redact or hash before storage). For POCs we recommend synthetic or redacted datasets; for production we integrate with customer data-masking pipelines.
- Q: What SLAs and support tiers are available?
  - A: Hosted: standard support with published uptime targets. Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; response and escalation per enterprise support tier. Private: configurable support with on-call options.
- Q: Do you perform penetration testing?
  - A: Yes — Redwood runs regular internal and annual third-party penetration tests. Summaries available under NDA.
- Q: Who owns the model outputs and telemetry?
  - A: Customer retains ownership of their data and outputs. Telemetry required for billing and performance tuning is accessible via console and APIs; customers can request deletion per data retention policies.

Operational playbook snippets (ops & enablement):
- SE enablement kit: 1) one-week internal ramp with product engineer, 2) scripted POC runbook with load generator, 3) templated discovery memo, 4) security package bundle (DPA, SOC2 summary, network diagram).
- Escalation matrix: include primary SE, solutions architect, customer success manager, and head of enterprise success. Attach PS engagement SLA for technical escalations.

Ownership & next steps:
- Playbook owner: Maya Patel (GTM enablement).
- Required reviews before publish: Security, Legal, and Sales Ops.
- Action items:
  1) SEs: validate the POC checklist during next 3 deals and provide feedback.
  2) AEs: adopt pricing guardrails and route any discount >35% to Sales Ops.
  3) PM/Product: update the performance benchmark table quarterly.

Appendix: Useful CLI/commands & references
- Example quick trace extraction (CLI):
  - redwoodctl traces export --service inference --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-01-07 --format json
